period_label: Research review as at 8 September 2026 · no enacted uniform national ward-fund programme
source: National Government Constituencies Development Fund Act, 2015 (as amended 2022/2023); County Wards (Equitable Development) Bill, 2024 (Kenya Parliament, not enacted); illustrative county-specific Ward Development Fund legislation (Nairobi City County, Kiambu County, Kakamega County revenue-allocation/appropriation Acts)
refresh_trigger: Replace this closure if Parliament enacts a uniform national ward-development-fund law (such as a future enactment of the County Wards (Equitable Development) Bill) that establishes one comparable ward-level allocation formula, or if every one of the 47 counties independently adopts a directly comparable, officially published ward-fund allocation series sharing a common definition, unit and fiscal period that could be assembled into one governed 1,450-ward series without fabricating or estimating any county's figure.
reason: Kenya's only nationally uniform constituency/ward-adjacent development fund is the National Government Constituencies Development Fund (NG-CDF), established and governed by the National Government Constituencies Development Fund Act, 2015 (as amended in 2022 and 2023 following the Supreme Court's August 2022 ruling that the pre-amendment Fund was unconstitutional for intruding on devolved county functions). The Act allocates and administers the Fund per constituency: Section 4 sets the national allocation formula against the 290 constituencies, and Part VI establishes one National Government Constituency Development Fund Committee per constituency to manage it. There is no ward-level NG-CDF allocation, disbursement or committee. Separately, a number of county governments have created their own 'Ward Development Fund' or 'Ward Fund' programmes through individual County Assembly Appropriation/Revenue Allocation Acts — for example Nairobi City County (increased from KES 1.4 billion to KES 2 billion across its 85 wards for FY2023/24), Kiambu County (a KES 600 million Ward Fund Bill signed into law across its 60 wards), and Kakamega County (KES 1.2 billion, about KES 20 million per ward, across its 60 wards) — with several other counties (including Embu, Nandi, Kisumu, Machakos, Murang'a, Meru, Laikipia and Nakuru) reported to have created or be creating comparable schemes. These are distinct county-specific administrative programmes created under different County Assembly Acts, with different total amounts, different per-ward formulas, different fiscal years and different governance rules; they are not present in all 47 counties and are not consolidated into one comparable national table. A national bill that would create one uniform statutory ward development fund — the County Wards (Equitable Development) Bill (most recently tabled in 2024, with an earlier 2018 version) — remains before Parliament and has not been enacted as at this review. Because no single official, uniform, nationally comparable ward-level development-fund programme currently exists across all 1,450 statistical wards, the Atlas does not construct one governed indicator value per ward. Dividing NG-CDF constituency allocations by ward count, treating an individual county's Ward Fund programme as if it were a national series, silently leaving the slot blank, or fabricating a value for counties that have not published one would each violate the cascade contract's prohibited shortcuts (never divide a parent total by arbitrary shares merely to fill child slots; never manufacture a value where none exists). The slot is therefore closed as not applicable rather than approximated, and will be revisited only if the underlying legal/programme landscape changes as described in the refresh trigger.
